Industrial Design
The professional service of creating and developing concepts and specifications that optimize the function, value, and appearance of products and systems for the mutual benefit of both user and manufacturer.

Interaction Design
The focus is upon how people interact with technology. The goal is to enhance people’s understanding of what
can be done, what is happening, and what has just occurred.

Experience design
The practice of designing products, processes, services, events, and environments with a focus placed on the quality
and enjoyment of the total experience.

What principles does interaction design draw upon
psychology, design, art, and emotion to ensure a positive, enjoyable experience

Human-centered design
The process that ensures that the designs match the needs and capabilities of the people
for whom they are intended

What do great designers produce?
pleasurable experiences

What is discoverability?
how to work a product, Meaning discovering what it does, how it works, and what operations are possible.

What are the five fundamental psychological concepts of discoverability?
affordances, signifiers, constraints, mappings, and feedback.

What is an affordance?
An affordance is a relationship between the properties of an object and the capabilities of the agent that determine just how the object could possibly be used.

What does glass affords?
glass affords seeing through and support, but not the passage (movement through) of air or most physical objects
(atomic particles can pass through glass).

what is anti-affordance?
The prevention of interaction.

What is a signifier?
Signifiers communicate where the action should take place. (Signifiers are signals.)

What is the difference between an affordance and a signifier?
Affordances determine what actions are possible. Signifiers communicate where the
action should take place. We need both.

What is mapping?
The relationship between the elements of two sets of things.

What is an example of natural mapping?
For example, to move an object up, move the control up.

Natural mapping takes advantage of what?
spatial analogies, leads to immediate understanding

What is feedback?
communicating the results of an action

Feedback must be immediate.
True

What is a conceptual model?
an explanation, usually highly simplified, of how something works

Conceptual models are not inferred from the device itself.
False

What is the system image?
The system image is what can be derived from the physical structure that has been built (including
documentation)

What is the paradox of technology?
The same technology that simplifies life by providing more functions in each device also complicates life by making the device harder to learn, harder to use.
Major Areas of design are industrial design, interaction design, and experience design.

FIGURE 1.7.Good Mapping: Automobile Seat Adjustment Control. This is an excellent example
of natural mapping. The control is in the shape of the seat itself: the mapping is straightforward. To
move the front edge of the seat higher, lift up on the front part of the button. To make the seat back
recline, move the button back.

Conceptual models are often inferred from the device itself.
Some models are passed on from person to person. Some come from manuals. Usually the device itself offers very little assistance, so the model is constructed by experience.

The designer’s conceptual model is the designer’s conception of the look, feel, and operation of a product. The
system image is what can be derived from the physical structure that has been built (including
documentation). The user’s mental model is developed through interaction with the product and the
system image
